Question:
Let \(f\) be a function with the following properties:

(i) \(f(1) = 1,\) and

(ii) \(f(2n) = n \cdot f(n)\) for any positive integer \(n.\)

What is the value of \(f(2^{100})?\)
Solution:
The input is a power of 2, so repeatedly applying the rule will eventually reach the known value \(f(1)=1\). First choose \(n=2^{99}\):
\[
f(2^{100})=2^{99}f(2^{99}).
\]
The next application contributes a factor \(2^{98}\), and each further application halves the input again. Continuing all the way to 1 gives
\[
f(2^{100})
=2^{99}\cdot2^{98}\cdots2\cdot1\cdot f(1).
\]
Multiplying powers with the same base adds their exponents. Since \(f(1)=1\), this becomes
\[
f(2^{100})=2^{1+2+\cdots+99}.
\]
To sum the exponents, pair them from the ends: \(1+99=100\), \(2+98=100\), and so on. There are 49 such pairs and the middle term 50, giving
\[
1+2+\cdots+99=49(100)+50=4950.
\]
Therefore \(f(2^{100})=\boxed{2^{4950}}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
